title: Add cross-tool composite-key conformance coverage
description:
Rationale:
shape and rvl both consume profile key lists, so correctness depends on shared tuple semantics even though their domain outcomes differ. A reusable conformance surface should prevent either tool from narrowing to the first component, flattening tuples with colliding sentinels, or drifting in per-component normalization.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Define the shared ordered-tuple rules: ASCII-trim each component, any empty component is incomplete, missing-token strings remain literal key bytes, equality and ordering are lexicographic over component byte strings.
- Add reusable fixtures or helpers covering repeated first components, reordered rows, duplicate full tuples, empty secondary components, non-UTF-8 bytes, and sentinel-collision tuples.
- Assert machine output exposes authoritative component arrays while joined labels remain display-only.
- Wire the conformance coverage into both shape and rvl consumers or document the minimal consumer integration contract.
- Bump the crate version if the reusable API changes.
close_reason: Added reusable and live cross-tool composite-key conformance coverage with version bump.

comments.author: Zac
comments.text: Added spine-rules 0.2.0 composite-key conformance API and fixture corpus; executable assertions cover per-component ASCII trim, incomplete components, literal missing tokens, repeated first components, structural sentinel collisions, non-UTF-8, duplicate tuples, component order, and lexicographic ordering. Added authoritative JSON component-array/display-label assertions and a live shape+rvl pipeline across reorder/change, duplicate, and empty-secondary cases. Also fixed upstream child reaping in pipe_tools and made the existing rvl value assertion explicit. Validation: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy -- -D warnings; cargo test (19 passed, 3 doctests ignored); git diff --check. UBS reviewed: findings are intentional assertion panics and caller-selected subprocesses in this test-infrastructure crate.

title: Consume cmdrvl/evidence-protocol for conformance over protocol objects; add cargo-deny boundary ban on evidence-machine
description:
DECISION (Zac, 2026-09-15; canon: cmdrvl-context docs/02-architecture/evidence-machine.md §2 "Protocol origination and boundary rules"): the Evidence Protocol wire types live in a dedicated PUBLIC package `cmdrvl/evidence-protocol`. spine-rules stays the conformance/rules layer — it CONSUMES evidence-protocol; it does not become the protocol package. operator.v0 stays here.

DELIVER:
1. Add `evidence-protocol` as a dependency once the crate exists (path dep during bootstrap, then crates.io/git tag). Do not copy or re-declare any *.v0 type here.
2. Conformance rules over protocol objects, only as consumers appear — first candidates: R-xxx inquiry.v0 validates against schema + refuses ambiguous universe/completion; receipt.v0 has all four axes populated (execution, domain_disposition, coverage, claim_state); plan.v0 hash equals blake3 of canonical JSON; answer.v0 coverage totals reconcile (total == sum of terminal states). Each rule cites the consuming code in evidence-machine (em-3h0 / em-13q / em-36x). No speculative rules (AGENTS anti-conformance-metastasis).
3. Dependency-boundary check: add `deny.toml` (cargo-deny) banning crate `evidence-machine` and any git source under `github.com/SaltIO/`; wire `cargo deny check bans sources` into CI. Provide the same snippet as a reusable rule/template so every public operator repo (canon, shape, rvl, fingerprint, profile, verify, benchmark, twinning, decoding, crucible) can adopt it; file follow-ups there only when they first depend on spine-rules ≥ this version.
4. README: one paragraph on the three-layer split (evidence-protocol = types; spine-rules = rules + operator.v0; evidence-machine = private runtime) with the one-way dependency diagram from canon.

ACCEPTANCE: `cargo deny check` green with the ban present and a negative test (a fixture Cargo.toml adding evidence-machine fails the check); at least one protocol conformance rule with a passing and a failing fixture; no *.v0 struct defined in this crate (grep test).
